pending.title: How Frogs Swallow
pending.hook: Frogs swallow their food using their own eyeballs
pending.narration: Frogs swallow their food using their own eyeballs. It sounds crazy, but it is true. Frogs do not have teeth to chew their meals. Because they cannot chew, they need help pushing food down their throats. So, they pull their big eyeballs deep down into their heads to force the food down. Without blinking, they actually cannot swallow at all. Hit follow for more fun facts.
pending.caption:
I just found out how frogs eat and I am honestly a little creeped out.

They do not have real teeth to chew their food like we do, so they swallow everything whole. Back in 2004, researchers at the University of Idaho watched this happen and proved that frogs literally cannot swallow without blinking. Their eyeballs sink so far down into their mouth cavity that they act like little pistons to shove the food down. It is like using your own eyes to push a sandwich down your throat.

Would you want eyeball pistons if it meant you never had to chew your food again? 🐸
